questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants**

 
 
• Plants are not considered a direct element of weather.
 
• While vegetation can influence local climate conditions (like temperature and humidity through transpiration and shade), they are a component of the ecosystem or biosphere.
 
• Plants are affected by weather elements and can, in turn, have some impact on the immediate surroundings, but they are not a primary atmospheric variable used to define weather.
 
• Weather describes the state of the atmosphere at a specific time, whereas plants are living organisms that inhabit a region and are influenced by the prevailing climate and weather patterns.
 
• The distribution and types of plants in an area are more closely related to climate, which is the long-term average of weather conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Temperature**

 
 
• Temperature is a fundamental element of weather.
 
• It refers to the degree of hotness or coldness of the atmosphere at a particular time and place.
 
• Temperature is measured using instruments like thermometers and is a key factor influencing other weather elements.
 
• Variations in temperature drive atmospheric circulation and affect phenomena like precipitation and wind patterns.
 
• Daily and seasonal changes in temperature significantly impact human comfort and agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Humidity**
 
 
• Humidity is another crucial element of weather.
 
• It refers to the amount of water vapor present in the air.
 
• Humidity is typically expressed as relative humidity, which is the percentage of water vapor in the air compared to the maximum amount the air can hold at a given temperature.
 
• High humidity can make the air feel warmer due to reduced evaporation of sweat, while low humidity can lead to dry skin and discomfort.
 
• Humidity plays a vital role in the formation of clouds, fog, and precipitation.
 
 
 
• **Rainfall **
 
 
• Rainfall is a key element of weather, also known as precipitation.
 
• It refers to water falling from the atmosphere to the ground in the form of rain.
 
• Rainfall is a crucial component of the water cycle and is essential for sustaining life.
 
• The amount, intensity, and duration of rainfall are important characteristics used to describe the weather at a particular location.
 
• Rainfall patterns vary significantly across different regions and are influenced by factors like atmospheric pressure, temperature, and wind systems.

questions.question: The minimum temperature of the day occurs generally ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**in the early morning**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The difference between high and low temperatures on the same day is called Diurnal temperature variation.
 
• **During the day, the air temperature increases as energy gains exceed the energy lost from Earth’s surface and during the night, the air temperature decreases as Earth’s surface loses more energy than it receives.**
 
• **The minimum temperature of the day usually occurs in the morning. Hence option 4 is correct. **
 
 
• **The maximum temperature occurs in the afternoon.**
 
 
 
• The average temperature on the Earth will be around 14ºC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Andaman and Nicobar islands are located near the equator and so they receive day and night equally throughout the year.
 
• **Near the equator, the sun’s rays are nearly perpendicular and concentrated over a smaller surface area causing warmer temperatures.**
 
• Both the Arctic (North Pole) and the Antarctic (South Pole) are very cold because they do not get much direct sunlight.

questions.question: What does El Niño refer to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hot water current.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• El Nino is a surroundings layout that depicts the **odd warming of surface waters in the Japanese tropical Pacific Ocean.**
 
• El Nino is a **weather circumstance** that happens in the Pacific Ocean.
 
• **El Niño refers to a hot water current.**
 
• It is characterized by the **periodic warming of sea surface temperatures across the central and east-central Equatorial Pacific.**
 
• The term El Niño (Spanish for 'the Christ Child') refers to a warming of the** ocean surface, or above-average sea surface temperatures**, in the central and eastern tropical **Pacific Ocean.**
 
• The low-level surface winds, which normally blow from east to west along the equator (“easterly winds”), instead weaken or, in some cases, start blowing the other direction (from west to east or “westerly winds”).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Gulf Stream
 
 
 
• The Gulf Stream is a strong ocean current that brings warm water from the Gulf of Mexico into the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• It extends all the way up the eastern coast of the United States and Canada.
 
• The Gulf Stream is caused by a large system of circular currents and powerful winds, called an oceanic gyre.
 
 
 
 

 West Wind
 
 
 
• A current in the southern hemisphere moving from west to east at approximately 40°-55°S, caused by prevailing western cold winds.
 
• It encircles the earth, crossing the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific oceans
 
 
 
 

 Peru Current
 
 
 
• Peru Current, also called Humboldt Current, cold-water current of the southeast Pacific Ocean, with a width of about 900 km (550 mi). It is relatively slow and shallow.
 
 
 
 

 West Australian Current
 
 
 
• It is a relatively cold surface current of the southeast Indian Ocean, part of the general counterclockwise movement in the southern section of that ocean.

questions.question: The ozone layer is found in which of the following layers of the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stratosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone layer:-**

 
 
• **It is a layer of gas in the stratosphere that protects the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.**
 
• It is primarily made up of ozone molecules and is located approximately 10-50 kilometers above the Earth's surface.
 
• The ozone layer is important for the survival of various species on Earth, including humans, as prolonged exposure to UV radiation can lead to skin cancer, cataracts, and other health problems.
 
• The depletion of the ozone layer is primarily caused by human-made chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) that have been used in refrigerants, aerosol sprays, and other industrial processes. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troposphere, mesosphere, and exosphere, do not contain significant amounts of ozone and are not responsible for protecting the Earth from UV radiation. **

questions.question: "Eskimos" are associated with which geographical region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polar Region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Eskimos are the indigenous circumpolar people who have traditionally inhabited the northern circumpolar region from eastern Siberia (Russia) to Alaska (United States), Canada, and Greenland (Denmark).
 
• **Polar Region**
 
 
• The part of the Earth's surface forms a cap over a pole; characterized by a frigid climate.
 
• There are two main polar regions in the world, which are the Arctic and the Antarctic.
 
• The Arctic Circle and Arctic Tundra are found at the North Pole, and it covers nearly 5 million square miles of the 
 
• top of the Northern Hemisphere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arid Region**

 
 
• An arid region, also known as a **desert**, is defined by a severe lack of available water, to the extent of hindering or preventing the growth and development of plant and animal life.
 
• This harsh environment is typically characterized by extremely l**ow rainfall, high temperatures, and high evaporation rates**.
 
• Due to the **scarcity of water**, the biodiversity in arid regions is lower compared to other ecosystems. 
 
 
 
• **Savanna Grassland**
 
 
• Savanna grasslands in Brazil are called Campos__.
 
• These grasslands lie between 24°S and 35°S, which includes **Uruguay and parts of Paraguay, Brazil, and Argentina**.
 
• These are rich in plant species and are more diverse than forest ecosystems.
 
• The climate here is subtropical humid and the rainfall is distributed regularly all over the year.
 
• A grassland is an area that mostly comprises grasses.
 
 
 
• **Tropical Rainforest Region**
 
 
• The tropical rainforest is a forest with tall trees in a region of year-round high temperatures where an average of 50 to 260 inches of rain falls yearly.
 
• The tropical rainforests are confined to areas of heavy rainfall.
 
• Such areas are in the Western Ghats, upper parts of Assam, Tamil Nadu coast, and the island groups of Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar.
 
• Areas that receive more than 200 cm of rainfall and have a short dry season are the best area for the tropical rainforest.

questions.question: During October — November, the apparent movement of sun is towards the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**South.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** apparent movement** of the **sun **during** October and November** is towards the** South.**
 
• This is because during these months, the **Earth is tilted away from the sun** in the **Northern Hemisphere **and **towards the sun** in the **Southern Hemisphere.**
 
• As a result, the sun appears to move towards the South, and the **days become shorter** in the Northern Hemisphere and** longer** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the **winter solstice** and occurs around** December 21st **in the Northern Hemisphere and** June 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **movement of the sun** is caused by the** Earth's rotation on its axis **and its **revolution **around the sun.
 
• The Earth's axis is tilted at an** angle of 23.5 degrees **relative to its orbit around the sun, which** causes the seasons.**
 
• During the **winter solstice**, the tilt of the Earth's axis is at its **maximum,** causing the** least amount of daylight** in the Northern Hemisphere and the **most amount of daylight** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The opposite occurs during the **summer solstice,** which happens around** June 21st** in the Northern Hemisphere and** December 21st** in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• During the **equinoxes**, which occur around **March 20th and September 22nd, **the tilt of the Earth's axis is perpendicular to the sun, causing **equal amounts of daylight and darkness** all over the world.

questions.question: At the beginning of November, the depression condition shifted over the Bay of Bengal. The transfer relates to a cyclical asset that generates rain above ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The term **"depression"** is likely referring to a type of weather system known as a tropical cyclone,** which is characterized by low-pressure areas with strong winds and heavy rain.**
 
• **The Bay of Bengal **is a large body of water located in the northeastern part of the **Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and other nearby countries.**
 
• The transfer of a depression condition over the Bay of Bengal can refer to the movement of a tropical cyclone from one location to another within or near the Bay of Bengal.
 
• This transfer of a** depression condition can have significant impacts on the surrounding areas, including heavy rainfall, strong winds, storm surges, and flooding.**
 
• It's important to note that tropical cyclones are a natural occurrence and can't be directly linked to cyclical assets that generate revenue.
 
• **The Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea** are both **located in the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, between India and Southeast Asia.**
 
• During the monsoon season, which typically lasts from **June to September, **the region experiences heavy rainfall and strong winds.
 
• However, sometimes** a depression of winds can occur, which is a weather system characterized by low atmospheric pressure **and winds rotating around a center.
 
• When a depression forms over the** Bay of Bengal or Andaman Sea, **it can bring **heavy rainfall and strong winds to the surrounding areas.**
 
• The depression can also lead to the **formation of cyclones or tropical storms**, which can cause damage and disruption to coastal regions.
 
• The intensity of a depression can vary, with some causing only mild weather disturbances and others causing more severe weather events.
 
• **The Indian Meteorological Department closely monitors the formation and movement of depressions in the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea,** and issues warnings and advisories to help people prepare for any potential impacts.

questions.question: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical climate region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hurricanes primarily form in the tropical climate regions due to warm ocean waters and favorable atmospheric conditions.
 
• The tropical climate region provides consistent heat and humidity, crucial for the development and intensification of hurricanes.
 
• Most hurricanes originate in the Atlantic Ocean, particularly in the area known as the hurricane belt, which lies within the tropical climate region.
 
• The warm sea surface temperatures in the tropics, generally above 26.5°C, provide the energy needed for hurricanes to form and strengthen.
 
• Regions such as the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and the western Atlantic Ocean are common origins for hurricanes, all of which are situated in the tropical climate zone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tropical Cyclones**

 
 
• These are large-scale storm systems with a well-defined center and are characterized by strong winds and heavy rain.
 
• The term "hurricane" is used in the Atlantic and Northeast Pacific, while "typhoon" is used in the Northwest Pacific, and "cyclone" in the South Pacific and Indian Ocean.
 
 
 
• **Formation Factors**
 
 
• Six main factors are necessary for the formation of hurricanes: warm ocean waters, atmospheric instability, high humidity, Coriolis force, a pre-existing disturbance, and low vertical wind shear.
 
 
 
• **Hurricane Season**
 
 
• The Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, with the peak occurring between mid-August and late October.
 
 
 
• **Impact Zones**
 
 
• Regions most affected by hurricanes include the southeastern United States, the Caribbean, Central America, and parts of East Asia.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change**
 
 
• Climate change is believed to influence the frequency and intensity of hurricanes, with warmer oceans potentially leading to more powerful and wetter storms.

questions.question: Which among the following wind is associated with extreme cold and dryness?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Polar Easterlies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Polar easterlies are dry, cold prevailing winds that blow from the east.
 
• They emanate from the polar highs, areas of high pressure around the North and South Poles.
 
• Polar easterlies flow to low-pressure areas in sub-polar regions.
 
• Westerlies are prevailing winds that blow from the west at mid-latitudes.
 
• These winds are also called trades winds because winds blow from subtropical high-pressure belts towards the equatorial low-pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Seasonal winds

 
 
• The winds which change their direction in different seasons.
 
• For example, the monsoons in India are seasonal winds. 
 
 
 
• Local winds
 
 
• This wind flow are caused by the uneven heat of the Earth's surface within a small area.
 
• Local winds form only when strong winds are weak.
